title: Condensed model listing - version badges and ownership CTA
body:
Summary:
This note captures a lightweight, condensed model-listing card pattern for the catalog view focused on: compact visual density, immediate signal for pinned/version-stability, and a prominent ownership CTA (who owns this model in the org). The outcome should be a single-row friendly card that works at 3 density breakpoints (desktop wide table, compact cards grid, mobile stacked list).

Goals:
- Reduce vertical scanning time for platform users searching for a model to pin or route to an endpoint.
- Surface version staleness and rollback/fallback readiness in one glance.
- Provide a low-friction way to claim or contact an owner (ownership CTA) without needing to open the full detail panel.
- Keep cards keyboard-accessible and readable at small sizes.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not replacing the full model detail page; this is a discovery/listing pattern only.
- No new backend fields required beyond: model_id, latest_version, pinned_versions (list length), stability_label (stable / experimental / deprecated), owner (name + slack/email), telemetry: last_deployed_at, avg_latency_ms. If missing, display graceful fallback copy.

Wireframe notes (visual language):
- Layout: horizontal card with 5 primary regions: 1) model icon & name, 2) version badge group, 3) quality indicators (stability, perf badge), 4) ownership CTA, 5) quick actions (pin/preview/more).
- Dimensions: target 52px row height for compact, 72px for normal density. Avatar/icon 32px. Use truncated name with tooltip.
- Version badges: show up to 2 badges inline (e.g., "v2.1.0" and "v1.7.3 (fallback)") with a small chevron that expands an inline popover listing all pinned/compatible versions. Badges use color semantic: green=stable, amber=experimental, red=deprecated.
- Stability indicator: microcopy under model name: "stable for chat and generation" or "experimental: evaluate before production". Keep it one short sentence.
- Ownership CTA: a pill-shaped button reading either "Owned by Elena M." or "Claim ownership" depending on owner field. Hover shows contact options (Slack, Email). Clicking "Claim ownership" opens a small modal with a one-click claim + optional note.

Microcopy drafts (variants):
- Ownership CTA variants:
  - "Owned by {name} — contact" (compact)
  - "Claim ownership" -> modal title: "Claim model ownership" with helper: "Claiming makes you the primary contact for rollouts and alerts. Read-only viewers can still request changes."

- Version badge hover copy:
  - Primary: "v2.1.0 — last deployed 2025-10-19 — default for endpoints"
  - Fallback: "v1.7.3 — fallback used if v2.x out of capacity"

- Stability microcopy options:
  - Stable: "Stable — production tested, minor updates only"
  - Experimental: "Experimental — may have breaking changes"
  - Deprecated: "Deprecated — scheduled for removal, migrate"

Edge cases and fallbacks:
- Missing owner: show "Claim ownership" CTA and a small help icon linking to doc: "How ownership impacts routing & alerts".
- No pinned versions: show "No pinned versions" with a secondary action to "Pin latest".
- Long model name: truncate to 40 chars, tooltip shows full name and link to model detail.
- Offline telemetry: if last_deployed_at unavailable, hide latency metric and show passive state "telemetry not available".

Accessibility notes:
- Version badges must be keyboard focusable and announce full version text via aria-label.
- Ownership CTA uses role=button and provides dialog with focus trap for claim modal.
- Color should not be the only signal for stability (include iconography + text).

Performance & metrics to track (post-ship):
- Time-to-pin: median time from catalog view open to a model being pinned by user. Goal: reduce by 20% vs current.
- Owner contact click rate: % users who use contact after seeing owner CTA. Target: 10% in first month.
- Claim flows abandoned: monitor drops in modal flow.

Acceptance criteria / QA checklist:
- Compact row renders correctly at 320px, 480px, 1280px widths.
- Version popover lists full set of available versions and allows quick pin action.
- Claim ownership modal validates user permissions and writes owner metadata.
- Microcopy text matches copy doc variations below.
- Keyboard-only users can reach all actions and use the popover.

Copy appendix (final candidate copy; prefer short forms for compact UI):
- Ownership pill: "Owned by {First Last}" (if owner exists) / "Claim ownership"
- Stability prefix: "Stable: " / "Experimental: " / "Deprecated: " followed by 3–5 word rationale.
- Version badge labels: single token like "v2.1.0" with hover expanded text.
- Fallback label: use parentheses: "(fallback)" not red text.

Backlog grooming notes (priority sorted):
1) [P0] Inline version popover + quick-pin action (owner: Jonah) -> needs API endpoint to pin a model version for org-level default. Jira: CONSOLE-1123.
2) [P1] Ownership claim modal + permissions check (owner: Asha) -> tie into OCIM identity / team mapping.
3) [P1] Compact card responsiveness tweaks (owner: Product UI) -> add QA tickets for mobile.
4) [P2] Small telemetry surface (avg latency) with tooltip explaining sampling windows.
5) [P3] Add 'stability' auto-classifier in onboarding flow for models without stability_label.

Handoff notes for design-engineering pairing:
- Deliverables from design: final card spec (Figma frame), icon set (stable / experimental / deprecated), microcopy variants (finalized strings).
- Deliverables from eng: API endpoints for: fetch compact listing (include owner, pinned_versions, stability_label), patch ownership, patch pinned_versions. Must return minimal payload to enable quick list rendering.
- Suggested experiment: A/B test showing owner pill vs contact icon only to measure click-through and support requests.

Open questions (needs PM decision):
- Should claiming ownership automatically create alert subscriptions for the claimer? (security/consent implications)
- Do we allow org-level owners vs team-level owners (and display both)?
- Preferred default for missing stability label: assume "experimental" or show "unclassified"?

References and inspiration:
- Slack thread: #console-catalog (link: slack://channel?team=T123&id=C456)
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/289 (version popover prototype)

Next steps (this sprint):
- Sync with Jonah and Asha to split P0 work (this week).
- Drop Figma stub for compact rows into the "Console components" file; tag eng.
- Write a short Confluence page with decision on ownership semantics and alert opt-in (owner: Marta).

Notes to self (drafty):
- Keep copy minimal; research shows small pills with owner names increase trust and speed.
- If we route contact clicks to Slack DM, ensure we log consent for notifications.

End of note.
